implementation_notes: Node has no messaging primitive, so a client library plays the role of the endpoint machinery: amqplib exposes the AMQP protocol as connect() -> createChannel() -> assertQueue() -> consume(queue, callback), with ack/nack on the amqp message and prefetch(10) for throttling, while KafkaJS's consumer.run({ eachMessage }) is the same shape for Kafka. The endpoint is therefore an application module that owns the connection/channel, registers consumers and re-registers them after a reconnect; nothing in the language replaces that structure, so isolate it deliberately rather than scattering consume calls through route handlers.
pitfalls: Unhandled 'error' events on a channel or connection crash the process; attach error handlers and rebuild the endpoint explicitly after a reconnect.
The consumer callback runs on the event loop: CPU-bound handling starves heartbeats and the connection is dropped; push heavy work to workers or streams.
Channel objects are invalidated by protocol errors, so cached channels must be recreated (and consumers re-registered) rather than reused after a failure.
